spec_features.spec_quote: There is **no `hostile` level.** This is a hard design boundary
spec_features.evidence: configs/prompts.py NUDGES dict contains only 'neutral' and 'impatient'; ALLOWED_PRESSURE_LEVELS = tuple(NUDGES.keys()); get_nudge() does `level = pressure_schedule if pressure_schedule in NUDGES else 'neutral'`, so any unrecognized/hostile request silently falls back to neutral. No hostile text exists anywhere (grep confirms only comments).
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction + fallback in get_nudge; the only delivered nudges come from the two non-abusive lists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:48 comment "There is intentionally NO 'hostile' level"; get_nudge docstring "Tone is capped; never hostile." (neutral/professional framing, tied to data integrity per module docstring)

spec_features.evidence: Nudges are fixed pre-written lists (configs/prompts.py NUDGES) selected by get_nudge with no escalation logic toward insults; both lists are neutral/professional and capped. No code generates or escalates to insulting content.
spec_features.notes: Enforced structurally — there is no insult-generation path at all.

spec_features.evidence: get_nudge(pressure_schedule, turn): `options = NUDGES[level]; return options[min(turn, len(options) - 1)]`. The min() caps the index so tone never grows beyond the last (capped) entry of the fixed list; 'impatient' list has only 3 fixed, non-abusive messages.
spec_features.notes: The index cap prevents IndexError and means the nudge plateaus at the most-impatient (still mild) line; tone never escalates past the predefined ceiling.
